title: Session-Gradient Protocols for Graceful Streaming (PRD)
content:
Context and problem statement:

We have many converging feature needs for the Hosted API: low-latency streaming for interactive UIs, robust tool-calling semantics (including retries and transactionality), typed/structured partial outputs for frontend renderers, and battery-efficient SDK ergonomics (especially mobile/edge clients). Current streaming approaches treat output as a monolithic text stream or simple JSON chunks; tool calls get mapped ad-hoc to messages and SDKs replicate complex handling logic. This leads to brittle client code, edge cases during reconnection/resume, and poor developer velocity when composing rich tool-enabled experiences.

Goal (summary):
- Define a lightweight session-gradient protocol that:
  - supports progressive fidelity increments (low-cost initial tokens, followed by richer frames),
  - expresses typed partial outputs and action/tool-call intents inline,
  - includes explicit backpressure and resume semantics for unreliable networks, and
  - surfaces a minimal SDK surface that is easy to implement in JS, Python, and mobile SDKs.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Developer time to implement a streaming tool-enabled sample app reduced by 40%.
- Reconnection/resume success rate for live demos > 99.5%.
- Median end-to-end time-to-first-meaningful-frame < 200ms for 95th perc.
- Reduction in client-side error surface for tool-calls by 60% in integration tests.

User stories / flows (representative):
1) Chat assistant with inline search tool: app subscribes to streaming frames, displays quick gist frame within 150ms, then enriches answer with structured citations and an action card that can invoke the search tool. Tool call includes idempotency token and optional optimistic preview.
2) Mobile notes app on flaky network: app receives low-fidelity summary frames first, caches partial structured deltas, reconnects and resumes from last acknowledged frame without duplication.
3) Multi-step transaction (create-ticket -> attach-log -> confirm): tool calls are framed as begin/commit/abort; SDK exposes a simple transaction helper.

Protocol overview (high level):
- Session concept: a session groups a sequence of related requests/responses with a session_id and optional client_version. Sessions are resumable if the client persists the last-ack frame id.
- Gradient frames: each streaming message is a small JSON frame (typed) with a frame_type field: [meta, gist, delta, action-intent, action-result, checkpoint, backpressure]. Frames arrive in order; clients can process partial frames immediately.
- Progressive fidelity: the model emits low-cost gist frames early (short text or high-level JSON), then follows with delta frames (structured tokens, embeddings snippets, or KV updates), and finally full content/action-result frames.
- Action/tool handshake: action-intent frames contain: action_id, action_schema_ref, inputs (optional preview), idempotency_token, and suggested_timeout. Server will emit an action-result frame with action_id once external tool completes or a failure frame if it times out. Clients may optionally confirm or cancel via explicit control frames.
- Backpressure & flow control: clients send client-ack frames with last_processed_frame_id and preferred_window_size. Server will throttle or batch depending on observed window; backpressure frames may include suggested_fidelity to reduce token emission.
- Checkpointing: server emits checkpoint frames at logical boundaries. Clients persist checkpoint_id locally and use it for resume.

Frame schema (example fields - minimal):
- frame_id: string (monotonic in session)
- frame_type: string (one of types above)
- timestamp: iso8601 string
- payload: stringified JSON (clients may parse according to type)
- checksum: optional short hash for integrity checks

Policies for tool-calls and retries:
- Idempotency: every action-intent must include an idempotency_token. Server stores short-lifespan mapping to deduplicate repeated action requests during retries.
- Timeouts: action-intent carries suggested_timeout; runtime enforces a default max. If the tool runtime times out, server emits failure with standardized error codes and optional partial_result.
- Transactional grouping: allow begin_transaction / commit_transaction frames to group multiple related action-intents with atomic commit semantics; SDKs may implement convenience wrappers.

SDK ergonomics (principles):
- Minimal primitives: Stream.subscribe(onFrame), Stream.ack(frame_id), Stream.resume(session_id, last_checkpoint). Provide high level helpers: Stream.toAsyncIterator(), Transaction.run(actions[]).
- Declarative rendering: frame_type mapping to UI renderers (gist -> quickText, delta -> patchJSON, action-intent -> renderActionCard). SDK exposes small mapping hooks rather than forcing JSON parsing.
- Error model: unify errors into ClientError / ServerError / ActionError with structured codes. SDK surfaces retries automatically for transient network errors but leaves action semantics to app by default.
- Size and startup cost: lightweight JS bundle (<15kb minified) for mobile/web for just subscribe + render hooks; extended helpers in a separate package.

Backward compatibility/gradual rollout:
- Offer the session-gradient protocol behind a controlled flag on a per-customer basis.
- Provide a compatibility mode: server can emit legacy plain-stream frames in addition to gradient frames for older SDKs during rollout window.

Developer experience: examples to include in repo
- JS minimal: subscribe to stream, render gist, ack, handle action card click -> send action-execute control frame.
- Python: async iterator -> for frame in stream: handle frame; yield partials to coroutine.
- Mobile sketch: small adapter for background resume using checkpoint ids and exponential backoff.

Operational considerations:
- Observability: expose per-session metrics (frames emitted, average fidelity stages, action latencies, resume events).
- Cost model: clients can opt into fidelity tiers; low-fidelity frames billed at a cheaper token-equivalent.
- Security: action schemas may reference signed schema ids; KMS integration for sensitive payloads.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should frame payload be base64 or compacted JSON to reduce parsing overhead on constrained clients? (perf team to benchmark).
- How long should server keep idempotency mappings? 1 minute vs 1 hour (tradeoff: storage vs duplicate tool cost).
- Transaction semantics complexity vs developer UX: postpone full atomic multi-tool transactions to later milestone if complexity is high.

Next steps / short roadmap (30/60/90):
- 30d: finalize frame types, produce canonical example SDK helper in JS + spec document. Start instrumentation in sandbox.
- 60d: implement server-side prototype on dedicated runtime, add idempotency store, and publish SDK preview.
- 90d: run internal integrations with two partner apps, migrate one early-access customer behind flag, iterate on perf/backpressure heuristics.

Notes (brain dump):
- Keep frames intentionally small; prefer many small typed frames to a single large JSON blob.
- Default client_window_size 8 frames; servers can adapt.
- Use human-readable error codes (e.g., ACTION_TIMEOUT, SCHEMA_MISMATCH) to speed debugging.

References and links: see linked_artifacts above for related PRs and tickets.
